name: Kolum So Dogon
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Retired glottocode: split 2011 into Ampari (aqd) and Mombo (dmb); look under successor codes (dogonlanguages.org domain now hijacked)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages kolu1247 (Bookkeeping) and momb1254 (refs: Heath 2016 Penange grammar, Campbell et al. 2022).
sources.note: Bookkeeping record; no descriptive references for kolu1247, none for Mombo beyond classification.

sources.citation: Прохоров, К. Н. 2022. Тональный изафет в момбо [Tonal ezafe in Mombo]. Вестник СПбГУ. Востоковедение и африканистика 14(3): 449-468. DOI 10.21638/spbu13.2022.305.
sources.note: p. 450: 'Момбо — тональный язык с двумя уровневыми тонами — высоким (H) и низким (L).. TBU выступает мора' (two level tones, mora = TBU, contour tones on bimoraic syllables); nothing on stress/accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/ударен/акцент = 0).

sources.citation: Прохоров, К. Н. 2021. Относительные конструкции в момбо [Mombo relative constructions]. Rhema. Рема 2021(1): 76-98. DOI 10.31862/2500-2953-2021-1-76-98 (CC BY 4.0).
sources.note: Syntax/tonosyntax of internally headed relatives; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2014/2015. Dogon lexical tones of stems. Unpublished cross-Dogon typology note, 6 pp., dogonlanguages.info.
sources.note: p. 3: in southwestern Dogon (Bunoge, Penange, Ampari, Mombo) all verb forms have tones predictable from the inflectional form, no lexical melodies; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Prokhorov, Kirill. 2012. A Grammar of Mombo, Songho dialect (Dogon, Mali). Draft, September 2012, ix+275 pp. dogonlanguages.org / cdstar EAEA0-8597-35C6-7E30-0.
sources.note: Phonology chapter is fragmentary: 3.2.2 'Metrical structure of bisyllabic stems' is mora-counting (short = 1-2 morae take {H}, long = 3+ morae take {HL} in possessed nouns and 3SG perfectives) and 3.7.2 verb tone; zero occurrences of 'stress' or 'accent'; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Hochstetler, Lee (SIL Mali). 2010. Change Request 2010-018: split [dkl] Kolum So Dogon into Ampari Dogon [aqd] and Mombo Dogon [dmb] (adopted 2011-05-18). 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistics only (Mombo-Ampari 40-53 percent), Prokhorov quoted 'separate non-intercomprehensible varieties', sec. 4(c) 'No existing literature.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger [& Douyon, Denis]. 2005 [printout 8 July 2012]. Ambaleenge of Kema, a language of the Dogon group in Northern Mali and its affinities. Draft wordlist paper, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge (= Glottolog ref 47983).
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 3: 'Ambaleenge of Kema has two tones, High and Low.' No statement on stress or accent. (Ambaleenge = Mombo variety of Kema per Hochstetler 2010 and dogonlanguages.info.)

sources.citation: Hochstetler, J. Lee, J. A. Durieux & E. I. K. Durieux-Boon. 2004. Sociolinguistic Survey of the Dogon Language Area. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2004-004, 189 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; identity only: Mombo 'is called kolu-so by Donno-so speakers'; Calame-Griaule 1956:66 'Ces deux dialectes [Mombo, Ampari-kora] sont reunis par les Dogon du centre sous le nom de kolum so'; DNAFLA 1982 map uses kolu so for Mombo.

sources.citation: Moran, Forkel & Heath (eds.). Dogon and Bangime Linguistics (dogonlanguages.info, MPI-EVA CLLD), language page 'Mombo' and bibliography table (330 records).
sources.note: 'Mombo (exonym Kolu So).. Nyambeenge and Ambaleenge varieties reported on Blench's website.. may turn out to be dialects of Mombo'; bibliography lists only Prokhorov's 2012 grammar draft, 2008 dictionary and conference talks for Mombo, nothing for Ampari.

sources.citation: Heath, Jeffrey. Field notes / lexicon on Ampari (Dogon Languages Project; dogonlanguages.info lists lexicon only, no grammar).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: No Ampari grammar or sketch exists; if the DLP ever posts one it would supersede everything here for the Ampari half of the retired code.

sources.citation: Prokhorov, Kirill. Any later or fuller version of 'A Grammar of Mombo' (the 2012 draft lacks chapters 3.1-3.6 of the phonology) or his RAS Institute of Linguistics dissertation on Mombo tonosyntax (RFBR project 19-312-90051, 2019-2021).

sources.note: The 2012 draft's phonology chapter is unwritten except for metrical (moraic) structure and verb tone; a complete phonology chapter would hold the stress statement if any exists.

sources.citation: Prokhorov, Kirill. 2011. Tonal head-marking in the Mombo noun phrase. In Afrikanische Sprachen im Fokus: linguistische Beitraege zum 19. Afrikanistentag (Koeln: Ruediger Koeppe), 209-222.
